theorem_title: The Unique Games barrier is exceeded on the three-occurrence Horn class (83/84 above 0.94616 and 0.94017)
natural_language_statement: Let $\beta^\star=0.94016567$ and $\alpha^*=0.94615981$ be the Unique Games thresholds for MAX 2-SAT and weighted MAX-$\{1,2\}$-HORN-SAT. Then $\beta^\star<\alpha^*<\tfrac{83}{84}$ and $\alpha^*<\tfrac{19}{20}$; for every $d\ge6$, $19(3d+3)<20(3d+2)$, i.e. $\tfrac{3d+2}{3d+3}>\tfrac{19}{20}>\alpha^*$; and for every $D\ge3$, every $D$-regular graph $G$ with a port labelling on $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, with independence number $\alpha$, and every independent set $I$ with $6\alpha\le7|I|$, the assignment obtained from $I$ satisfies $$84\cdot\operatorname{sat}(T_G)\ \ge\ 83\,\bigl((D+1)n+m+\alpha\bigr),$$ that is, at least $83/84$ of the optimum $(D+1)n+m+\alpha$ of the three-occurrence Horn formula $T_G$. For $D=3$ the hypothesis $6\alpha\le7|I|$ is the independent-set size guaranteed by the Berman--Fujito cubic-MIS algorithm (item (3) of Theorem `thm:ugc-broken`); the guarantee itself is not part of the statement. The Unique Games thresholds quantify over all instances, so the statement concerns a bounded-occurrence class and is consistent with the Unique Games Conjecture. The bounded-occurrence guarantee of Ghoshal--Huang--Lee--Makarychev--Makarychev (items (1) and (2)) is cited in the paper and is not formalized.
explanation: The threshold comparison is a numerical check (`norm_num`, `PaperArithmetic.ugc_thresholds`), and $(3d+2)/(3d+3)>19/20$ for $d\ge6$ is `omega`. For the last part, `DegreeFormula.lift_ratio_from_mis` gives $(21D+20)\,\mathrm{opt}\le(21D+21)\,\mathrm{sat}$ for a $6/7$-approximate independent set, and for $D\ge3$ one has $83(21D+21)\le84(21D+20)$, which yields $83\,\mathrm{opt}\le84\,\mathrm{sat}$. This submission is supported by a Lean 4 formalization, available at https://github.com/frankvegadelgado/paloma. The formalization covers the exact optimum identities, the repair and lifting steps, and the arithmetic of the approximation ratios. The Goemans–Williamson, Berman–Fujito and Trevisan guarantees are taken from the literature and are stated as explicit hypotheses; the Unique Games thresholds are cited in the paper and are not formalized.
